Good change of pace! This lad has a good knack of doing this! Bowls the back of the hand delivery, Smith reads it late but does well to keep it out in the end. Bairstow walks up to the stumps and shares some words of wisdom with Smith.
Shortens his length now, served it outside off, SS stays back in defense.
Nice shot! Fuller in length outside off, Smith unfurls a textbook front foot defense towards the off side. Solid as a rock, says Bill Lawry on air.
Harmless ball, too wide outside off to make the Aussie skipper play at it.
Drops it on a back of a length does Curran, Steven Smith hangs back and with a full face of the bat he punches it towards cover.
Drags his length back, outside off, punched into the cover region.
Goes very full and bowls it wide on off, Warner leans forward and across and bunts it towards the short cover fielder who dives to his right to make a stop.
Sprays it a touch wider outside off, Warner leans forward and pushes it gently towards cover.
Good ball! Woakes fires it full on the stumps, it's pretty full and there is a hint of it tailing back in. David Warner moves his leg out of the way and jams it back on the bounce towards the bowler.
Once again, slants it away, this time on a back of a length, Warner defends it away from the body towards cover.
Woakes changes the angle and goes over the wicket. He angles it away on the fourth stump line, Warner has no qualms in leaving that one alone.
Chris Woakes to continue from the other end.
Shaping in substantially from a length, Smith sits deep in the crease and remains composed in his defense.
On a good length around off, defended solidly off the back foot.
Bowls it fuller outside off, tempting Smith to go for an audacious shot. He remains circumspect in approach and leans forward to push it to covers.
Starts off with a length delivery right on the money. It is swinging in appreciably. Smith hangs back and defends it stoutly.
We are back and so are the players on the field after a slight delay. Steven Smith on strike, Tom Curran to complete his pending over. Here he comes...
1420 local time update - There is some good news, folks! It has stopped raining and the covers are coming off. Play is scheduled to resume at 1430 local time, provided the rain stays away.

Australia wouldn't mind. Conditions are conducive for swing bowling and you have to be on your toes all the time. The hosts have only scored 16 from 68 balls post-lunch and it is especially Warner who has gone into a shell. Shows that it has been tough work for the batsmen. England, on the other hand, have been right on the money. They will hope that there is a resumption soon. They are in the driver's seat at the moment. Stay with us for more updates...

1400 local time - Sadly, the drizzle has picked up now. Not threatening but enough to force the players out of the field. The weather forecast was not good for today and the rain has finally arrived. The radar shows that it will continue for a while but seems that the weather will clear up after that. The 22-yard strip has been covered. Let's keep our fingers crossed!
Short of a length ball, defended solidly off the back foot to covers.
On a good length on leg stump, Warner hops and tucks it through backward square leg for a single.
Fullish ball on off, Smith shuffles across and taps it to mid off.
Good length delivery in line of the stumps, defended solidly off the back foot.
Woakes goes wider of the crease and angles in a length ball. Smith has it covered and blocks it solidly.
Short of a length ball outside off, Smith hangs back and punches it to short cover.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Fullish delivery outside off, a hint of away shape on that. Smith leans ahead and strokes it to short cover.
Angling into Warner who tucks it to mid-wicket.
Nicely disguised! Back of the hand slower ball outside off, Warner winds up for the cut but ends up chopping it to covers.
Short of a length around off, negotiated nicely off the back foot.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

David Warner has gone into a defensive mode in this innings. He has played out 9 maidens so far, the most he has ever done. Don't know whether it is a correct ploy. Playing your natural game might be the way to go but let's see if Warner comes out on top.
Length delivery outside off, not changing its course. Warner makes an assured leave.
Back of a length ball on middle, Smith rises with the bounce and tucks it away around the corner for a single.
Straying on the pads, tucked to fine leg for a single.
Short of a length around off, Steven Smith shuffles a bit and blocks it to short cover.
Good yorker from Woakes, Smith is sharp as a hawk and digs it out with utmost ease.
Length delivery, angling in. Kept out off the back foot.
It has gone pretty gloomy. Dhamasena looks a little concerned. Might be a bit of drizzle in the air.
On a length well outside off, Warner has room to work with and pushes it to sweeper cover for a run.
Straighter this time, on middle, Smith nudges it behind square on the leg side for a single.
Chris Woakes comes into the attack.
Slower ball on a full length outside off, Warner reads it well and makes an assured leave. England are back to bowling maidens.
On a length outside off, holding its line. Warner plants his front foot across and lets it go.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Similar length ball, David stays deep in the crease to keep it out.
Back of a length outside off, skidding after pitching. Warner hops and lets it go.
Full ball outside off, Warner has his feet moving and pushes it to covers.
This is testing stuff from Anderson. Bowls a sharp short ball around the rib-cage area, Warner is caught in a tangle and fends it off through fine leg for a run.

Runs coming after a long time! Back of a length outside off, Smith places it through point. The fielder hares after it and puts in a slide near the fence to keep the ball in play. Saves a run for his side. Huge cheer from the MCG crowd.
Fuller in length around off, eased off the front foot to covers.
Short of a length ball, shoots off the deck. Smith hops and tucks it towards mid on.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

Beautifully bowled! Tailing in on middle, Smith plays it with soft hands to square leg. If he missed that, he would have been a candidate for an LBW. However, Smith rarely misses such deliveries, he is a class act.
Full length ball outside off, David shows good composure and allows it through. Fourth consecutive maiden. England building up pressure.
Fuller in length, pushed off the front foot to mid off.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.

The on-air commentators make a good comparison. The ball on which Khawaja departed, it came in initially and then nipped away. He didn't have his feet moving and was caught by surprise. In contrast, Warner in the previous over played out a similar ball with a lot of authority. He moved his back leg across and defended it solidly. Shows how important playing with the correct approach is.
Back of a length outside off, Warner stays back and blocks it solidly.
Similar ball around off, Smith works it in front of square leg for a single.
On a length on off, Smith opts to stay back and keeps it out to mid-wicket.
Tom Curran returns for a burst.
Back of a length outside off, patted off the back foot to cover-point.

Well bowled and well played as well! Anderson goes wider of the crease and bowls a good length ball in the fourth stump channel. After pitching, the ball moves away a touch. Warner with an exaggerated shuffle defends it to the off side. This is what good bowlers do. They keep on mixing things up to keep batsmen on their toes.
On a drivable length outside off, Warner doesn't get tempted into a false stroke and once again remains circumspect in approach.
Oh.. that kept a bit low! On a length on off, Warner adjusts in the crease to keep it out watchfully.
Similar length ball in that probing off stump channel, David has it covered and blocks it solidly. He has been very watchful in this innings.
On a length well outside off, angling in. Warner covers his sticks and allows it through safely.
Short of a length ball outside off, left alone by Steven. Consecutive maidens for England, good stuff from them.
Full ball outside off, Smith drives it sweetly but once again finds Malan who dives to his right to make a good stop.
Smith will be disappointed with that as a boundary was there for the taking. Low full toss outside off, Steven reaches out to it and times his push well but finds Malan in the point region.
Length delivery in the fourth stump channel, shaping in a shade. Smith leans ahead and defends it with his bat close to his pad.
Similar length ball, shaping in from outside off. Smith hops and defends it stoutly towards covers.
Back of a length ball wide outside off, pretty harmless. Smith leaves it alone.

Warner knows that it will be difficult to pierce the packed off side field and hence, shuffles a touch. Works it to mid-wicket but won't get a run as a fielder is stationed there. A disciplined maiden from Anderson.
Anderson bangs the deck hard and bowls it around off. Warner rises with the bounce and taps it with an angled bat face to point. Anderson is bowling according to his field.
Short of a length ball in the zone of apprehension, Warner shuffles across and watches it sail through to the keeper.
Good length delivery on off, David plays it with soft hands to mid-wicket and shouts 'No' to his partner.
In the zone outside off, Warner knows where his off stump is and makes a good leave.
Angling in substantially on a length from outside off, Warner has it covered and tucks it defensively towards mid-wicket.
Smith is looking in good touch now. Strides ahead just a touch and drives it sweetly to covers.
Well bowled! Very full on off, there is a bit of nibble in the air. Warner does well to dig it out towards deepish mid on and scurries across to the other end.
The field on the off side gets packed again as Warner is on strike. Broad switches his angle to around the wicket as well.
Nice timing! Fullish ball outside off, Smith leans into it and just pushes it past extra cover for a run. Wants the second but it is not really on.
Similar length ball well outside off, shaping away a touch. Steven is in no mood to fiddle with it.
After getting hit for a boundary, Broad naturally shortens his length and keeps it outside off. Smith shuffles across and makes an assured leave.

FOUR! Beautiful! Smith is such a treat to watch when he is in the zone. Shuffles a bit to the half volley and drives it crisply down the ground. No chance for mid off to cut it off and the ball whistles away to the fence.
Stuart Broad to continue from the other end. A breeze is blowing across the ground.
Sits deep in the crease to the length delivery and buries it into the track.
Angling in sharply, pushed off the front foot to extra cover.
Good length delivery in the zone of apprehension, leaving the southpaw after pitching. Warner points his bat skywards to allow it through.
Anderson shortens his length, Warner gets behind the line of the ball and defends it solidly to covers.
Anderson steams in again and delivers a full ball around that probing off stump channel. Warner prods forward and blocks it.
Good shot for no runs! Overpitched outside off, Warner crunches the drive but it goes straight to the man at mid off.

We are back for the afternoon session. The conditions are overcast at the moment and the ball will move around. David Warner and Steven Smith to continue their innings. James Anderson to bowl first up after lunch. Here we go...
... Day 4, Session 2 ...

Warner and Bancroft started cautiously and it was the latter who started playing positively after getting a hang of the track. The right-hander failed to carry on though and was dismissed by Woakes - Another Australian batsman who chopped it on, the fourth to be precise. Khawaja at No. 3 showed intent but Anderson came back to send him packing with a beauty. The visitors are still ahead by 94 runs but the good thing for Australia is that their most reliable pair, Warner and Smith is battling it out. If the visitors manage to dismantle one of them early, there is a possibility of the home side crumbling under pressure. With the ball already reversing, expect a cracking contest in the middle. Join us shortly.

Another session which has been won by England! They continue to dominate the proceedings. Though they would have wanted their last wicket partnership to add some more runs but they wouldn't be complaining as their bowlers have come out and responded well. It was a change in tactics from Joe Root as he rotated his bowlers around and gave them short bursts which worked in his favour.
Back of a length ball on off, Steven Smith rises with the bounce and answers it with a straight bat. That's LUNCH on day 4, Australia trail by 94 runs!

Ooh... almost another wicket! Smith has to be careful. Broad is mixing it up really well. Bowls this on a length in the corridor of uncertainty and the ball holds its line. Smith expects it to move in and goes for an expansive drive but at the last moment, the ball seams away to whizz past the outside edge of his bat. That was so close.
Broad shortens his length and bowls in the corridor on off. Smith hops and keeps it out.
Overpitched on middle and leg, Smith digs it out to the man at mid on.
In the zone of apprehension, moves away a shade. Smith has it covered and makes a good leave.
On a length around off, Smith hangs back and does well to defend it with soft hands.
On a good length outside off, Warner leans ahead and taps it to covers.

Michael Clarke makes a good point on air. He says that Smith is very good as he stays leg side of the ball to negotiate the deliveries that are coming in. There are a lot of batsmen who have trouble in negotiating that as they tend to fall over and get trapped on the pads. But Smith is an exception.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Very full on leg stumps, Smith does well to place it through backward square leg. Fine leg does the mopping up job and keeps it down to a couple.
On a length and leaving the right-hander, Smith hangs back and defends it solidly.
Fullish delivery, driven crisply to mid off.
Length delivery middle on leg, Smith tucks it around the corner for a single.
Length delivery outside off, angling in. Warner makes an assured leave.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Similar delivery outside off, patted to extra cover.
Overpitched outside off, pushed nicely off the front foot to mid off.
Length ball outside off, Warner leaves it alone.
On a length around off, defended solidly off the front foot.
Length ball which keeps a bit low around off, Smith does well to block it. Excellent over from Anderson.
On a length just outside off, Smith lets it go.
Full ball outside off, eased off the front foot to covers.
Back of a length around off, pushed off the back foot to square leg.
Brilliant bowling! On a length on off and middle, stays a bit low. Smith is alert and does well to keep it out.
Steven Smith is the next man. He is in a purple patch with the bat and has scored 502 runs in this series so far. Can he play another substantial knock?

OUT! Edged and gone! The strike bowler brings in the reward and England continue to remain on top. Anderson is so good from around the wicket and the angle has worked for him. Bowls it on a good length around off, coming in with the natural angle but after pitching, the ball seams away. Khawaja has no choice but to play at it and an outside edge is induced. Jonny Bairstow moves to his left and takes a regulation catch. Smart thinking from England's premier bowler. The replays show that he was hiding the ball when he was running in and while delivering, the shiny side was on the outside. As a batsman, you don't have any idea which way the ball will move. These small things matter a lot in cricket. Another batsman fails to capitalize on the start. Australia trail by 99 runs and are in a spot of bother.
Good lines from Broad. In the corridor of uncertainty, Warner makes a good leave.
Fullish in length, a confident front foot push to mid off.
On a length in the zone of apprehension, Warner plants his front foot across and leaves it alone.
A man goes back to deep point for David Warner to cut off the boundaries.
Full ball on leg stump, Usman tucks it through square leg for a run.
That's a brute of a delivery. Coming in initially with the angle on a length and then straightens after pitching to fox Khawaja.
On a length just outside off, left alone.

Stuart Broad comes into the attack replacing Moeen Ali. Might have well stuck to Ali. You need to back your spinner, more so when he was looking in good rhythm earlier. A bad over shouldn't force a change.
Fuller in length, attacking the stumps, kept out from within the crease.
Full length ball on middle and leg, Warner keeps it out watchfully.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Full ball on off, patted back to the bowler.
On a length outside off, angling in, Warner makes an assured leave.
Fullish ball around off, Warner goes for a drive but gets it off the bottom half of the bat towards mid off.
FOUR! Khawaja is putting Ali out of his rhythm. Excellent use of the field again as he drives it crisply through mid off for a glorious boundary. 11 from the over.
Full outside off, jammed to covers.

SIX! What a way to get off the mark! This is good intent from Khawaja. He skips down the track to the tossed up ball around off and lifts it over long off for a big maximum. The replays show that a young man in crowd took a scorcher of a catch. His friends are congratulating him and have big smiles on their faces.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Slower through the air outside off, defended solidly off the front foot.
Full ball on middle, Warner lunges forward in defense.
Length ball outside off, a solid front foot defense from Usman.
Joe Root comes in the second slip position and there is also a man at short mid-wicket now.
Back of a length ball on middle and leg, tucked towards mid-wicket for a run.

That's a peach! Almost took the outside edge. He steams in from around the wicket and bowls a length delivery outside off, it is angling in initially but then shapes away after pitching. Warner has no option but to play at it and is beaten all ends up.
Shaping in substantially from outside off, Warner covers his off pole and makes a good leave.
On a length outside off, left alone.
Overpitched outside off, eased off the front foot to mid off.
James Anderson is back on. Good move from Root to bring his strike bowler on.
Drifting in once again, Khawaja does well to keep it out. A testing over from Ali.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Drifting in towards Khawaja and stays a bit low. The batsman does well to block it.
Flat and quick outside off, punched off the back foot to covers.
Very full outside off, driven to deepish mid off for a run.
Floated outside off, Warner plants his front foot across and lets it go.
Length ball angling across Khawaja who lets it go.
The ball is down the leg side but the batsman still goes after it.
Usman Khawaja comes out to bat. Second slip is standing pretty close.

OUT! Bowled 'em! Woakes is up and running. Look at the jubilation on his face! Bowls a good length ball around off, in the corridor of uncertainty and gets it to nip in a touch after pitching. Bancroft leans ahead tentatively and tries to defend it but gets an inside edge onto his pads. The ball then goes onto crash into the stumps. He was looking solid as compared to his first innings but fails to make it count. He is the fourth Australian batsman who has dragged it on in this Test.

FOUR! Beautiful stroke! Bancroft is playing positive cricket and it is working for him. Fractionally overpitched on middle, Bancroft clips it nonchalantly through wide mid on and away she whistles to the fence.
Full length ball, angling in appreciably. Bancroft leans ahead and blocks it stoutly.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Bancroft is nimble on his feet. Comes down the track and clips it to deepish mid on for a run.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.

Ian Chappell makes a good point on air. Moeen Ali is not getting enough revs on the ball and as a result, he is not being able to cause problems for the batsmen. If you can't beat a batsman in flight, it will be difficult to pick up a wicket.
Well bowled! Sliding in with the arm, Warner comes forward and strokes it to covers.
Leans ahead and taps this one to mid on for a brisk single.
Floated delivery around off, Bancroft lunges forward in defense.
Starts off with a loosener down the leg side, Bancroft misses his flick. A good take from Paine behind the stumps.
Time for spin. Moeen Ali comes into the attack. He has been off colour in this series so far but this track is providing assistance as we saw with Nathan Lyon. Can he strike?
Another full ball around off, defended solidly off the front foot.
This is good bowling from Woakes. He keeps it full and attacks the stumps, Warner is equal to the task and digs it out on the track.
Similar length ball, similar shot, same result.
Fractionally overpitched around off, David drives it crisply towards extra cover. Says Wait On! to his partner.
Well bowled! Yorker on middle, Warner is alert and does well to jam it out.
On a length outside off, Warner stays rooted to the crease and taps it to covers.
Time for Drinks...

FOUR! Lovely shot! We saw him playing one straight drive at the start and he does it again! This was even better. Curran keeps it full on the stumps, Bancroft is quick to bring his bat down and drive it back from where it came. Tom in his followthrough fails to stop it as the ball goes through his legs to the fence for a boundary.
Fuller ball outside off, Bancroft presses forward and drives it through the gap at extra cover. Picks up a brace.
Bancroft leans forward and across and nudges it towards mid on.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Fuller in length and on middle, bunted down to mid on for one.
FOUR! Gets one through the cover region! This should calm Warner's nerves! Curran pitches it up outside off, Warner makes room and drills it through extra cover for a rocketing boundary.
Back of a length on middle, defended from within the crease.

Confusion in the field and that allows Warner to take three! Woakes looks to bowl the yorker but it's a low full toss. David pushes it towards extra cover and calls for one. The man from extra cover moves to his left but then lets it be, thinking that Broad from mid off will stop. Both don't go after it and it goes through the gap. They take another couple.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

Inside edge on the pads! Good delivery! Woakes hurls it on a length, this one curls back in a bit, Warner sans any foot movement tries to push it away but gets an inside edge on the pads. Had he missed, could have been easily trapped in front.
Back of a length outside off, Warner looks to cut but chops it towards the off side.

There was a discussion going on between the overs. Anderson, Broad and Root went to the umpire and showed the ball to him as they had some issue with it. A chunk from one side was seen coming out but the umpire feels it is still good enough to continue...
Short and served a bit wide outside off, a back foot punch towards cover.

Good stop from Broad! Fuller in length and outside off, Warner leans forward and drives it towards mid off. Broad there dives full length to his left to stop it from crossing the fence. Only a single taken.
Good length delivery, just outside off, defended solidly.
On middle and leg, worked towards the fielder at mid on for nothing.
Very full on off, jammed out towards mid off.
Short of a length delivery outside off, Cameron Bancroft stands tall and hits it through cover-point. The fielder from point hares after it to stop a run for his side.
Ahead of a length and outside off, punched off the back foot towards mid off.
Another one straight to the man! This will frustrate Warner! He once again leans ahead to a fuller ball and drives it well but to no avail.
Finds the man again! Fuller in length and outside off, driven nicely but once again finds the man at cover.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Pitches it right up there outside off, David Warner drives it again but this time he finds mid off.
Fuller on off, Warner eases it towards the cover region.

Another good point on air being made, this time by Ian Healy. He discusses that on the last ball of the previous over, Warner usually would have gone for the square cut as it was short and on the fourth stump line but since the field was packed on the off side, he tried to pull it across the line. It went off the inside edge and with the pitch not being a true one, this isn't an ideal stroke to play.
Outside off, Warner has got nothing to do with that one.

Inside edge! Needs to be careful here Warner! Short and outside off, Warner tries to go for the pull but this one stays a touch low. He gets an inside edge as the ball rolls down to fine leg for a single. We saw three batsmen from the hosts' camp chopping it back on the stumps in their first innings.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Fuller on middle, worked wide of mid on for a single.
Another one on the money! Fires in a perfect yorker, tailing back in on middle, Cameron digs it out.

This one nearly kisses the off pole! Curran is bowling superbly here. He lands it on a fuller length, just outside off, Bancroft plants his front foot across before shouldering his arms. The ball nips back in sharply and goes just, just past the off pole. A brave leave?

Just over the stumps! That was mighty close! Curran bowls an inswinger, a bit shorter in length and it doesn't rise much. Bancroft crouches low to defend but gets a bottom edge which bounces and then just goes over the top of the stumps. So, so close.
Sprayed wider outside off, Warner is happy to leave it alone. A maiden for Woakes.
Back of a length delivery, angling away outside off, defended from within the crease.
Takes a stride forward and mistimes his drive towards mid off.
Good shot! Back of a length delivery, wider on off, punched off the back foot but straight to the man at extra cover. Warner yells, WAIT ON!
Is right behind the line to this length ball and defends it down.
Shortish and outside off, Warner stays leg side and looks to punch but mistimes it towards short cover.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.

NOT OUT! The on-field call stays. There is nothing on Hot Spot and the Snicko also doesn't spot anything! England waste a review! Curran bowls it short and keeps it outside off, Bancroft tries to cut it through the line but seems to have missed it as the ball goes into the gloves of the keeper. An appeal from Root who is at second slip but umpire S Ravi shakes his head. After a while, Root takes the DRS as he feels he heard something. Hot Spot shows no mark while there is no spike on Snicko as well. Joe walks towards the umpire and is seen having a word. Nevertheless, a review gone.
A huge shout for a caught behind. Root at second slip says he has heard something. He talks to his keeper, nothing from the bowler. And the English skipper signals 'T'! Is there a nick?
Stands tall and punches it towards the point fielder.
Shortish and angling in, Bancroft gets across and works it towards mid-wicket where the fielder makes a diving stop to save some runs.
Length delivery on middle and leg, tucked behind square on the leg side for a single.
Good length delivery, angling away, Warner gets across and defends it down safely.
Double change. Root is giving short bursts to his bowlers it seems. Tom Curran into the attack now. Just a slip in place for him.
Back of a length delivery on middle, defended towards the on side off the back foot.
Short of a length delivery, slanted across on the fourth stump line. Warner stands tall and fetches it from outside off to deep square leg for just a single. Was in complete control of that shot.
Angles it across the left-hander, Warner resists and makes a leave.
Good length delivery on middle and leg, worked gently towards mid-wicket.
A catching cover-point comes in place. A packed off side field for Warner.
Slants it away on a shorter length outside off, Warner taps it in front of cover, wants the single but won't get it.
Woakes begins with a short ball outside off, Bancroft punches it off the back foot through cover for a single.
An early change from Root. Broad is out and here comes Chris Woakes into the attack.
Good length delivery on middle and leg, Warner shuffles across and clips it through mid-wicket. It's in the gap again and he gets another couple. Good start for the Aussies.
David has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

A back foot punch! Stands tall to a length ball and punches it through the gap at cover. Two fielders give it a chase, Warner wants the third but Bancroft is late to respond. Will have to settle for a couple.

FOUR! Nicely done by Warner! Anderson slants it away on a length outside off, Warner just opens the face of the bat to guide it between the gap at first slip and the gully fielder for a boundary. Seemed to have gone off the edge but he intended to play there.
Good length delivery on middle and off, defended from within the crease.
Fuller in length and just outside off, stroked off the front foot towards mid off.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Too straight from Broad, clipped nicely off the pads to fine leg for a single.
Mid-wicket drops back to deep square leg. The weather has also become much brighter. Good signs!

FOUR! Classical! We saw a few from Cook when he was batting and now this young lad shows us what he has got. After a short one, Broad pitches it up but it's too full. Bancroft leans ahead and with a straight bat he drives it down the ground for back-to-back boundaries. Pleasing to the eyes stuff!
FOUR! Shot! Broad goes short, doesn't rise much and Bancroft is up for the task. He swivels just a touch and goes bang over mid-wicket with a pull shot. No need to run for those.
Shortish delivery on middle and off, Bancroft initially tries to duck but then at the last moment rises on his toes to defend.

Good point from Clarke on air. He fails to understand the logic behind keeping a deep point. Warner just taps it away and scampers through. This is the perfect time to put pressure, you have got enough lead on the board so attack as much as you can.
Good length delivery, angling across, Warner taps it towards point and crosses for an easy single.
Fuller in length and angling in on middle, Bancroft leans forward to push it away but gets it off the outer half towards cover.
Shortish ball, angling in on the body, Cameron is quick to duck under it.
Warner is off the mark as well! A bit shorter on middle, David hops and tucks it with soft hands towards mid-wicket for a quick single.
Good length ball on the stumps, Warner hops and tucks it towards mid-wicket.
Another watchful leave! Slanting away from a good length, David lifts his bat to make an assured leave.
Angling away from a length outside off, Warner takes his time as he watches it pass.
Good length delivery, sprayed a bit wider outside off, shouldered arms to.
Another bouncer but the line is again down the leg side, left alone without much fuss.
Bumper but it's down the leg side, Bancroft moves inside the line to leave it alone.
Broad goes fuller, angling in on middle, the batsman tries to push it but gets it off the inner half back to Broad.
Angling in from around middle and leg, Cameron shuffles across to keep it out with a straight bat.
Beautiful delivery to begin with! On a length and just around off, in that probing channel, Bancroft presses forward to defend but the ball whizzes past the outside edge to the keeper.
Stuart Broad to share the new cherry with Anderson. Two slips and good to see a bat-pad in place who is a bit deep.
That stayed a bit low! On a good length and on the stumps, Warner crouches low and keeps it out back to the bowler. Excellent first over.
The Barmy Army is on top of their voices and are seen singing in the stands. What is good to see is that the England skipper, Joe Root is singing along with them...
Good length delivery on middle and leg, Bancroft works it off the pads. Gets it off the inside edge down to fine leg to open his account. Australia are away.
Fuller and angling in this time, Bancroft moves a touch across and defends it towards mid on.
Another length delivery, with a hint of away movement, CB decides to shoulder his arms again.
On a length and just outside off, good lines from Anderson as Cameron makes a watchful leave.
Anderson hurls a length delivery from over the wicker, gets it to move away a shade, Bancroft shoulders his arms to that one.
